evidence.quote: The Re0.1Ta1.6W0.6(TaC)x refractory composite samples were prepared by vacuum arc melting using a DHL1250 vacuum arc furnace (SKY Technology Development Co., Ltd, China).
The ingots were re-melted eight times (melting current was 500–800 A, each melting duration was at least 3 min, and each interval was cooled for at least 5 min.) to ensure chemical homogeneity.

evidence.quote: The Re0.1Ta1.6W0.6(TaC)x refractory composite samples were prepared by vacuum arc melting using a DHL1250 vacuum arc furnace (SKY Technology Development Co., Ltd, China).

The diffraction data indicate that the phase composition of the Re0.1Ta1.6W0.6(TaC)x refractory composites include BCC phase (referenced to ICDD no. 04–004–9210) and Ta2C phase (ICDD no. 04–003–3788).
With increasing TaC content, both the size and volume fraction of Ta2C carbides increase, as measured from SEM images (e.g., 34.39 % for x = 0.35, 52.29 % for x = 0.5, and 66.65 % for x = 0.7).

evidence.quote: Similarly, the metallic BCC matrix is also continuous throughout the composite. This co-continuous distribution of the Ta2C ceramic phase and the BCC metallic phase results in a strong mutual constraint effect between the two phases.
All composites exhibit a co-continuous 3D network of BCC matrix and Ta2C phase.

evidence.section: 4.3. Influence of carbide on microstructure and its relationship with mechanical properties
evidence.quote: As TaC content increases, the volume fraction of the Ta2C also rises, accompanied by a near linear increase in yield strength. Based on Section 4.1, the Re0.1Ta1.6W0.6(TaC)x composites exhibit outstanding room-temperature and high-temperature strength, which can be attributed to the strengthening effect of Ta2C carbides.
